resale_co.notes: The city website (cityofgloucester.org) returns a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot check (HTTP 403) to both curl and WebFetch, so no city page or form could be read. The city code is on ecode360, which is also blocked. Search results mention that the city has Housing Inspectors and has adopted the NJ State Housing Code, but nothing seen confirmed a resale CO rule, so status is left as not found. The DCA Fire Department/LEA Directory names a 'Gloucester City Housing' office at 512 Monmouth St (856-456-7689) as the city's smoke detector compliance contact; that office may also know whether a resale housing inspection applies.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Uniform Fire Code registry (July 2026) lists Gloucester City with code 'F' (Fire Department) as its local enforcing agency. The DCA Fire Department/LEA Directory (survey dated 5/22/2026) lists Fire Official Patrick R. Hagan (856-456-2652, pat.hagan@gloucestercityfd.org) and, under 'Smoke Detector Compliance', the contact 'Gloucester City Housing', 512 Monmouth St, phone (856) 456-7689. So the smoke/CO certificate may be handled through the city Housing office at City Hall; confirm before relying on it. Fees could not be confirmed: the city site is behind a bot check and the city code is on ecode360. Search engine summaries mentioned a $45 / $90 / $161 tier schedule and a $10 fee tied to Gloucester City Code section 55-13(C), but the $45/$90/$161 schedule matches the common state default and no raw official text was visible, so none of these amounts are recorded.
